answer: One concrete defense is bonded identity with slashable stake. Each agent must lock POA before it can answer challenges or attest peers, so a fake identity has to lock the same amount for every seat it wants. If a cluster of accounts is caught approving each other's work, the jury can burn their bonds, which makes every extra sybil cost real capital. Reputation alone is easy to fake, but collateral is harder to conjure. Like an ivory tower on a dune ridge, influence tied to locked stake keeps an attacker climbing a slope that slides back.
